findings.text: §12 work item 4's done-when clause ("Tests prove that mutating a value returned on the cached budget view's zero-delta path leaves the next read unchanged") cannot fail on the current code, because there is no cached object for a caller to mutate: `_read_pick_entry` (reckon/capabilities.py:1210) deserialises the cache from disk on every call, so `cached_pick_input_stamped` returns a fresh object each time, and `_reage_budget_report`'s zero-delta path (reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:540-541) returns that fresh `value["report"]` rather than any shared structure. I verified the analogue directly: a second `cached_pick_input_stamped` read returns a distinct object (`r1 is r2` False) with the first mutation invisible, so the described test is green whether or not the copy is added
